summary: An excerpt from a fiction manuscript (Book 2, part 135) in which the narrator Cas, recovering from a gunshot wound, talks with Rio and then Arthur. Cas reflects that Rio's kindness may come from religious motives rather than affection, and that Rio shot him on purpose, a choice Cas defends as a nonlethal plan. Arthur is furious, insists the shot was lethal, and remains at Cas's bedside despite being upset with Rio.
one_line: Recovering from a gunshot, Cas defends Rio's shot against Arthur's anger while reflecting on whether religious kindness counts as friendship.
key_facts: Cas tells Rio he considers him a good friend, and Rio replies, "I'm not your friend, Cas."
Cas reflects that friends who save your life and care for you while you are injured act like friends, even if their reasons are not affection.
Rio saved the lives of everyone in the group, including Cas, according to Cas.
Cas says "I knew I could line up a nonlethal shot" after Rio shot him.
Arthur responds "He shot you!" and insists that "That was absolutely, positively a lethal shot."
Arthur says that if the bullet had not bounced and missed Cas's heart, Cas could have died.
Cas says "I made it bounce," and that "It bounced 'cause I told it to."
Rio is out when Cas first wakes enough to talk with Arthur.
Arthur says he will not leave Cas alone "with someone who shot you."
Cas says the only case Arthur was working on was Pithica.
Cas describes Arthur as having earlier swung between trying to get Rio sold into slavery and having a guilt breakdown over getting Cas killed.
Cas says the drugs have been taken away from him, which is why he cannot sigh without pain.
Cas tells Arthur that getting shot "was the plan" and that it "allowed Rio to" act, though the sentence is cut off.
